analysis:
Examined release-pipeline changes: dev-branch workflow_dispatch support in scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py (head lines 112-121), scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh (head lines 36-43), and CI routing test updates in scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py.

api.py: a dispatch on refs/heads/dev now follows the dev path. It requires RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev and a GitHub-verified commit on dev ancestry, and the new check at line 119 requires source == current dev head. This is stricter than the push path, which tolerates a moved dev head. A dev dispatch signs and publishes only a dev release and never reaches the staging or prod branches. Prod stays tag-gated: resolve-provider-release.sh line 74 still requires a tag for prod, and verify_workflow_source still verifies the signed tag for tag pushes. Dev-lane dispatch is limited to people who can dispatch workflows on dev, and the signer still checks verified commits. Dev builds use the -dev.branch.N version stamp, and validation_only is forced false. The dispatch cannot set a version override because the override is cleared, and the dev dispatch cannot select staging or prod because environment mismatch fails closed.

Pre-existing: a dev-branch commit does not require reviewed-master review. The existing design already allows this for dev push, and this PR only extends it to dispatch. Residual contract not visible in the supplied evidence: the downstream workflow (release-provider.yml) must route RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev for dispatches and keep prod signing identity unavailable to dev-branch dispatch. I could not verify this, so it is recorded as an integration question.

test-ci-component-paths.py: test-only changes covering label-gated PR CI (run-ci/run-gpu-ci), an unlabel job, cluster_gpu gating and PR path filtering. The corresponding workflow files are not in the supplied units, so I could not verify their permissions. The tests assert there are no secrets, environment or id-token usage in ci workflows. Possible concerns for a deeper pass: the unlabel job's token permissions, and the label-trigger path running PR code on self-hosted macOS runners. Those depend on workflow files not supplied here.
